title: memcg 与 cgroup：每个 App 的内存隔离和系统视图
key_conclusions: memcg provides a per-cgroup charge view that complements but does not replace smaps/PSS.
Shared page charging can identify who currently carries cost, but it does not prove producer ownership.
Global memory, app memcg, smaps, fd evidence, and lmkd timelines must be cross-checked.
Victim usefulness requires post-kill movement in memcg, global buckets, and PSI.
shallow_points: The article does not validate cgroup v1/v2 paths on real Android devices.
It does not include real memory.stat samples from app, system_server, and HAL cgroups.
It does not quantify shared page charge redistribution.
It does not include tooling to map pid, uid, and cgroup hierarchy automatically.
discovered_connections: Day 66's shared accounting ambiguity becomes clearer when memcg charge is compared with fd and smaps evidence.
Day 65's victim worksheet gains a per-cgroup charge and post-kill movement check.
Day 53's global bucket attribution must be paired with app-local memcg before assigning responsibility.
Day 68 should combine smaps, showmap, heapprofd, and memcg for Native/System attribution.
suggest_future_topics: Day 68 should focus on Native/System attribution using smaps, showmap, heapprofd, and memcg cross-validation.
A future tool should discover Android cgroup layout and collect memory.current/stat/events for all app pids.
A future appendix should compare cgroup v1, v2, and vendor custom memory nodes.
Day 71 should reuse memcg when evaluating multi-process app architecture costs.
knowledge_gaps: Need real device samples for cgroup v1/v2/mixed layouts.
Need examples of shared page charging and charge migration.
Need automated pid-to-cgroup and cgroup-to-package mapping.
Need measured memcg changes after lmkd kills producer versus consumer processes.
